name: Shipping chokepoints
value: 7 tankers hit since 16 Nov; traffic ~65% down
summary: Seven tankers hit near Hormuz since 16 Nov, per JMIC; strait traffic reported about 65% below pre-war levels
state: The Joint Maritime Information Centre said seven tankers had been hit since 16 Nov, and UKMTO reported two tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz on 22 Nov; shipping through the strait is reported to be about 65% below pre-war levels (Gulf News, 23 Nov). Hormuz crude flows averaged about 9.5m barrels a day in the 10 days to 19 Nov, down from 12.2m in October, per Kpler data (Trading Economics). A tanker was struck and caught fire in the strait on 20 Nov, and an Iranian tanker signal that appeared to cross the US blockade on 23 Nov was likely spoofed (Bloomberg via gCaptain). Hormuz traffic stays materially impeded.
for_you: Delays and higher freight and insurance costs can feed through to fuel and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO and JMIC guidance for the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded; 7 tankers hit since 16 Nov (JMIC); traffic about 65% below pre-war levels

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
